title: Acute exacerbation of COPD, 68-year-old man
provenance: Vignette written 2026-09-30 for the evaluation harness; expected answers extracted from the cited documents.

intake.complaint: Increased breathlessness and cough with more yellow sputum for 2 days.
intake.history: Ex-smoker, 40 pack-years. Known COPD on tiotropium inhaler.

triage.note: Both extractors: level 1. A: Primary triage Rapid Assessment, Respiratory Distress row: the Level 1 column (x~136, p4) lists 'SpO2 < 90% room air'. SpO2 88% meets it if it was a room-air reading; the intake does not say. Otherwise the adult Vital Signs Level 2 column (x~131, p7) 'SpO2 < 92%' applies. 'Wheeze, expiratory rhonchi; airway intact' is Level 3 in both primary triage (p4, x~356) and the SOB complaint row (p11, x~244). HR 104, RR 26 and Temp 37.9 are Level 3 (p7). MTS does not adjust for a COPD patient's usual baseline saturation. B: SpO2 88% is taken as a room-air reading, which falls in the Level 1 Rapid Assessment cell 'SpO2 < 90% room air' (x~136, p4). If it is judged a chronic baseline or an on-oxygen reading, the vital-signs cell 'SpO2 < 92%' (x~131, p7) gives Level 2. The intake's 'wheeze, expiratory rhonchi; airway intact' is a Level 3 cell (x~356 p4; x~244 SOB p11). HR 104, RR 26 and Temp 37.9 are Level 3 cells (x~244, p7). The most urgent applicable cell is chosen.

disposition.note: Admission indicated: older age, hypoxaemia, tachypnoea. General ward if he responds to controlled oxygen and bronchodilators. HDU/ICU if NIV is needed (hypercapnic acidosis) or the exacerbation is life-threatening. / He meets the admission criteria (older age, hypoxaemia, fever, likely infective cause). The ward is preferred. HDU/ICU is correct if ABG shows hypercapnic acidosis needing NIV, or if he deteriorates. RESUSCITATION_BAY is accepted only as the initial ED zone, because the MTS triage level is 1. Discharge is not acceptable: he is hypoxic at 88%.

adjudication.method: two independent extraction passes (A, B); agreed items scored

A: Triage Level 1 assumes the SpO2 of 88% was read on room air. If he was already on oxygen, it is Level 2.
The only source for admission criteria is the COPD CPG 2009 list (older age, significant comorbidity, failure to respond, etc.). ABG results will decide ward vs HDU.
Oxygen targets differ between documents: the COPD CPG says 90-93%, while MTS triage treats 92-94% as Level 3. The gold uses the CPG target.
B: Is SpO2 88% on room air? This decides MTS Level 1 versus Level 2. Chronic hypoxaemia in COPD may make Level 2 the more realistic reading.

The COPD CPG (2009) does not explicitly forbid uncontrolled high-concentration oxygen. It recommends controlled oxygen 'to avoid CO2 narcosis' and warns that outcomes are worse above SpO2 93-95% in hypercapnic failure. For that reason high-flow oxygen is not listed under drugs_forbidden; the adjudicator may want to add it.
The CPG's target is SpO2 90-93% (a 2009 document), while many clinicians write 88-92%. The regex accepts both.
